status: proposal — awaiting Chris approval; nothing restructured until approved

inputs.learner: Primary: graduate-level adult who recently came to faith; eager, analytical, near-zero biblical literacy; anxious that nuance means the faith is 'made up'; reads sequentially from wherever he lands and takes questions to a general chatbot. Also: casual adult learners; existing Christians and study groups.
inputs.site_intent: A connected library: full reader with a map, guided modules, and a Theologian that answers from the passage in front of the learner.

unit_pattern.intro: The question this unit answers, why it matters, and where it sits on the map (era, genre, place in the story)
unit_pattern.substance: Primary reading, then lessons; each reading skill is taught the first time a passage needs it; one visual anchor per unit
unit_pattern.checks: Teach one idea, then check it immediately; checks placed by subject fit, never batched at the end; no repeated items across units
unit_pattern.summary: What you now know, what Christians still debate, and which question carries forward
unit_pattern.apparatus: Footnotes/details: excluded gospels, Apocrypha, manuscript notes, extra-canonical sources, clearly labeled as outside the canon
unit_pattern.skip: Placement check per unit ('prove it to skip') for existing Christians; skipping is allowed in both directions

breadth: Module 1 is narrow and guided; each module widens scope, sources, and interpretive disagreement
